lead: Coinbase Global / COIN — the QR code that broke the app
smaller: Rivian / RIVN — follow Soros into the electric truck
Peloton Interactive / PTON — the takeover ticket gets torn up
Oil ETF / USO — chasing the seven-year-high war barrel
why_lead: The Super Bowl has now aired (13–14 February, before this cutoff), and its crypto ads produced the strongest crowd-attention evidence of the period: Coinbase's QR-code ad briefly crashed the app (CNN [[n0127]], Reuters [[n0852]], Investopedia [[n0851]], Notebookcheck/Snowden [[n1006]]), with Twitter reaction [[n0989]], Bloomberg's 'stop worrying and just buy crypto' [[n0905]] and FTX's 'Don't Miss Out' spot [[n0978]], against the Seattle Times finding that the ads did not drive downloads [[n0128]] and the Guardian's cigarette-advertising analog [[n1005]]. The card shows the gap the essay is built on: COIN only +0.37% to 195.25 USD and -15.12% over 20 sessions, BTC +0.92% to 42,586.92 USD, ETH -9.45% over five sessions. Relation to strictly earlier retail notes: crypto led on 2022-02-08 (Bitcoin rebound) and 2022-02-14 (Bitcoin, the pre-game Crypto Bowl). This lead is a material update rather than a carryover: a different instrument (the exchange, not the coin), and the outcome of the event the 14 February lead could only anticipate, resting entirely on evidence published after that cutoff; none of the 14 February lead's citations is reused, and the Smart Money View avoids the Saylor, TMX and KPMG items used by the 8, 9 and 14 February crypto items, citing Tiger Global's PDAX round [[n0957]] instead.
why_smaller: Rivian / RIVN: the day's largest US single-stock gain among retail names (+6.46% to 62.65 USD, Lucid +6.19%) with a simple follow-the-billionaire catalyst published 12–14 February (Soros stake: Reuters [[n0840]], MarketWatch [[n0839]], Notebookcheck [[n0771]]) and other filing-season stories (Burry [[n0818]], Munger margin debt [[n0849]], Mormon Church fund [[n0882]]). Relation to earlier notes: 2022-02-01 ran Netflix as follow-the-billionaires; this is a new stock and a new filing catalyst.

Peloton Interactive / PTON: kept as a brief secondary item (158 words) because Peloton was a smaller item on 2022-02-07 and 2022-02-08 and the 2022-02-09 lead. The update is material: on 14 February the new CEO said the company won't be sold in the foreseeable future (Forbes [[n0891]]) and the stock fell 5.33%, which retires the takeover-ticket framing of 7–8 February. Only evidence the 9 February lead could not use is cited (n0891, n0502, n0791, n0781, n0449); the job-cut, Blackwells, board and investor-slides items that edition used are not repeated.

Oil ETF / USO: the war-premium trade on new 14 February evidence (oil at seven-year highs on fears of an imminent attack [[n0135]], IEA revision [[n0909]], US gasoline [[n1983]]; WTI 95.46 USD/bbl, +2.53%). Relation to earlier notes: 2022-02-02 and 2022-02-08 ran Exxon Mobil and 2022-02-14 ran gold miners as hedges; this item uses a different vehicle (the crude barrel via USO) and centres on the non-confirmation by producers (XLE -2.36%, OXY -4.07%) and Iranian supply, kept secondary.
considered_not_chosen: Affirm / AFRM (-6.12% to 43.70 USD, -30.66% over five sessions): a continuation of the 2022-02-14 smaller item with no new own-date catalyst, so not repeated.
GameStop / GME and AMC (-5.76% and -5.64% on 14 February after the 5-session rally): AMC was a 2022-02-14 smaller item; the reversal carries no new attention evidence.
Moderna / MRNA (-11.68%): the biggest single-stock drop on the card but no own-date headline explaining it.
Upstart / UPST (+4.58% into results), Roblox and Airbnb: results pending on 15 February with no company-specific dated preview headline, so not used as a trade thesis.
Palladium (+6.96% to 2,342.50 USD/oz): large move without an own-date headline tying it to Russian supply.
Gold Miners ETF / GDX (+2.04%) and defence names (NOC -2.18%, LMT -2.33%): GDX ran on 2022-02-14; the defence reversal had no new catalyst.

Avoided as possibly after cutoff or misdated: n1502 (BBC Pidgin item on Russia withdrawing some troops from the border, stamped 14 February but describing the 15 February partial pull-back claim) and n1494 (CNN 'Photos: Russia invades Ukraine', a rolling page that cannot describe a pre-cutoff event).
